claim: The median survival from diagnosis of bone metastases has been reported to be very short in patients with lung cancer.
source: Although there have been many advances in treatment, the median survival from diagnosis of bone metastases has been reported to be very short in patients with lung cancer (Herbst et al., 2018; Knapp et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by citations to Herbst et al., 2018 and Knapp et al., 2022

claim: Exercise can improve survival and the quality of life in patients with cancer.
source: Many preclinical and clinical studies have shown that exercise can reduce the incidence of various cancers, inhibit cancer progression, reduce symptom burden, mitigate side effects of cancer treatment, and improve survival and the quality of life in patients with cancer (Bade et al., 2015; Ligibel et al., 2022; Pedersen et al., 2016; Schmitz et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to preclinical and clinical studies

claim: Exercise is safe perioperatively.
source: Exercise is safe perioperatively, and multiple international organizations have published exercise recommendations for patients with cancer (Bade et al., 2015; Ligibel et al., 2022; Stout et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citations to Bade et al., 2015; Ligibel et al., 2022; Stout et al., 2021

claim: The evidence to-date suggests a benefit of exercise in all stages of lung cancer and lung cancer survivors.
source: The evidence to-date suggests a benefit of exercise in all stages of lung cancer and lung cancer survivors (Bade et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to Bade et al., 2015

claim: Exercise has the potential to improve physical function and the quality of life in individuals with bone metastases and appears safe and feasible when it includes an element of supervised exercise instruction.
source: Exercise has the potential to improve physical function and the quality of life in individuals with bone metastases and appears safe and feasible when it includes an element of supervised exercise instruction (Ligibel et al., 2022; Weller et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citations to Ligibel et al., 2022 and Weller et al., 2021

claim: The optimal exercise prescription for patients with bone metastases is currently undefined.
source: The optimal exercise prescription for patients with bone metastases is currently undefined (Cavalheri and Granger, 2020; Stout et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citations to Cavalheri and Granger, 2020 and Stout et al., 2021

claim: The skeleton undergoes continuous remodeling throughout life, which is a balance between bone resorption by osteoclasts and new bone formation by osteoblasts.
source: Throughout life, the skeleton undergoes continuous remodeling, which is a balance between the resorption of mineralized bone by bone-resorbing cells (osteoclasts) and new bone formation by bone-forming cells (osteoblasts) (Wang et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by citation to Wang et al., 2022

claim: Osteocytes form an extensive interconnected network throughout the bone matrix termed the lacunar-canalicular network.
source: During this process, their morphology changes to stellate, facilitating the formation of an extensive interconnected network throughout the bone matrix termed the lacunar-canalicular network (LCN) (Prideaux et al., 2016; Robling and Bonewald, 2020; Schaffler et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to Prideaux et al., 2016; Robling and Bonewald, 2020; Schaffler et al., 2014

claim: Tumor cell dormancy is defined as an arrest in the cell cycle.
source: Tumor cell dormancy is defined as an arrest in the cell cycle (Blasco et al., 2022; Phan and Croucher, 2020).
evidence: Supported by citations to Blasco et al., 2022 and Phan and Croucher, 2020

claim: The details of niches and signals that support tumor cell dormancy in bone metastasis are largely unknown.
source: The details of niches and signals that support tumor cell dormancy in bone metastasis are largely unknown.
evidence: Stated as current knowledge gap in the field

claim: Bone destruction was found in the presence of bone metastasis in NSCLC patients.
source: Bone destruction was found in the presence of bone metastasis in NSCLC (Figure 1—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: Supported by H&E staining shown in Figure 1 supplement 1a

claim: The A549 migration ability was improved after co-culture with MLO-Y4.
source: We found that the A549 migration ability was improved after co-culture with MLO-Y4, with the promotional effect being much significantly stronger on co-culture with MC3T3-E1 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1e).
evidence: Supported by Transwell assay data shown in Figure 1 supplement 1e

claim: The promotional effect on A549 migration is much stronger on co-culture with MC3T3-E1 than with MLO-Y4.
source: We found that the A549 migration ability was improved after co-culture with MLO-Y4, with the promotional effect being much significantly stronger on co-culture with MC3T3-E1 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1e).
evidence: Supported by Transwell assay data shown in Figure 1 supplement 1e

claim: MLO-A5 cells inhibit the proliferation of NSCLC cells.
source: Moreover, MLO-A5, another osteocyte-like cell, also inhibited the proliferation of NSCLC cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1g).
evidence: Supported by CCK-8 assay data shown in Figure 1 supplement 1g

claim: The mechanically stimulated osteocyte sEVs have the most significant effect on the proliferation of NSCLC cells compared with SF and lEV components.
source: Moreover, the mechanically stimulated osteocyte sEVs had the most significant effect on the proliferation of NSCLC cells compared with SF and lEV components (Figure 4—figure supplement 1c and d).
evidence: Supported by CCK-8 assay data shown in Figure 4 supplement 1c and 1d
